item.title: AI Chip Startup Fractile in Talks for $6.5 Billion Value After Anthropic Deal
item.description: Fractile, a startup developing chips tailored for artificial intelligence use that has a deal to supply Anthropic PBC, is in advanced talks to notch a valuation more than six times higher than the price it landed in May.

item.title: Fed Minutes Show Many Officials Said Rate Hikes May Be Needed
item.description: Several Federal Reserve officials favored an interest-rate hike last month and many indicated that policy tightening would be necessary if inflation didn’t decline, a record of the central bank’s most recent policy debate showed.

item.title: Treasury’s Potentially Limitless Buybacks Cloud T-Bill Outlook
item.description: The US Treasury Department’s decision to boost buybacks of long-dated bonds is complicating the outlook for issuance of short-term securities, including Treasury bills, which are expected to be used to finance the plan.

item.title: OpenAI to Enhance Safety Processes for Paid Tool Customers
item.description: OpenAI said it will enhance safety processes for paying users who have access to its most advanced artificial intelligence models, stepping up its safeguards at a time when customers are entrusting AI with more complex tasks and sensitive information.

item.title: US, Canadian Funds Are Hedging FX Risks by Most in Three Years
item.description: Money managers in the US and Canada are increasingly hedging their currency exposure due to risks from trade, central bank and Middle East policy.

item.title: The New AI Bottleneck Might Not Be So Great For Investors
item.description: How safe are the AI lab protocols?

item.title: CPPIB Is Said to See Several Departures Across Senior Ranks
item.description: Canada Pension Plan Investment Board has seen several departures from its senior ranks over the past few weeks, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Goldman Sounds Out Investors for CoreWeave-Tied Data Center Bond
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc. is sounding out investor interest on a junk bond to fund construction of a data center leased to CoreWeave Inc., adding to a wave of borrowing tied to the neocloud firm as it seeks to capitalize on the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Stripe Agrees to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter; No Terms Disclosed
item.description: Stripe Inc. has agreed to buy OpenRouter Inc., an artificial intelligence startup that helps developers access and switch between AI models. No terms were disclosed.

item.title: ‘The Treasury Is Watching’: Bessent’s Buybacks Jolt Bond Market
item.description: A surprise US Treasury announcement on Wednesday is the most concrete evidence yet that the recent selloff in long-dated debt is concerning to Secretary Scott Bessent.

item.title: Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan’s Private Equity Boss Departs
item.description: Healthcare of Ontario Pension Plan’s global private equity head Lori Hall-Kimm is leaving to pursue another opportunity.

item.title: Ex-Meta Staffer Testifies Daughter, 14, Was Prey on Instagram
item.description: Arturo Béjar spent six years working on child safety tools at Meta Platforms Inc., but told a jury he did not fully understand the threats posed to young users on the platform until his 14-year-old daughter signed up for an Instagram account.

item.title: Venezuela Is Ready to Sign Oil Deals, Minister Tells Houston Investors
item.description: Venezuela is keen to sign production-sharing contracts and ramp up output from the world’s biggest crude reserves, Oil Minister Paula Henao told investors in Houston.

item.title: Lagarde Is Still Being Pursued by the WEF for Its Top Job
item.description: The World Economic Forum is still courting Christine Lagarde to take over as its next chair, an issue that was discussed at a meeting of the organization’s board this week, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Moderna’s 160% Surge Burns Shorts in ‘Painful’ $5 Billion Loss
item.description: A record surge in Moderna Inc.’s shares delivered a $5 billion blow to short sellers who had bet that the vaccine maker’s years-long slump would continue.

item.title: Two Sigma Lost a ‘Major Investor’ Over Co-Founders’ Feud
item.description: Two Sigma Investments’ billionaire co-founder John Overdeck said the quantitative hedge fund group lost a “major investor” due to his feud with co-founder David Siegel.

item.title: T-Mobile Cyber Staff Chopped Cable After Finding Chinese Hack
item.description: Salt Typhoon revelations inspired an internal investigation.

item.title: Carvana Rebounds as Report on Walter’s Pledged Stake Allays Fear
item.description: Shares of online used-car dealer Carvana Co. recovered some losses from a two-day selloff, after a report showed billionaire Mark Walter’s stake in the company was pledged, meaning he wouldn’t be able to immediately sell it as he contends with a federal probe of his investment empire.

item.title: SpaceX Is Unlocking More Shares. What That Means for Investors.
item.description: SpaceX’s blockbuster $86.2 billion initial public offering on June 11 smashed just about every record there is for new listings. Investors large and small rushed to buy shares in the IPO and get behind Elon Musk’s grand vision for data centers in space, expanded Starlink satellite internet service, artificial intelligence, computer chip manufacturing, space tourism and even asteroid mining.

item.title: Alibaba Tops Chinese Tech Stocks This Quarter on AI Resurgence
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. is reclaiming its place as one of investors’ favorite Chinese technology stocks, on bets it can beat rivals in the combative artificial intelligence market.

item.title: Google Pixel 11 Series Review: Familiar Design, Compelling Software Updates
item.description: The company’s new handsets bring a familiar design and some practical software and AI enhancements.

item.title: Ex-FTX, Alameda Executives Get 5-Year Trading Bans in CFTC Case
item.description: FTX co-founder Gary Wang and former Alameda Research Chief Executive Officer Caroline Ellison avoided financial penalties under a settlement with the US derivatives regulator over their roles at the collapsed cryptocurrency exchange.

item.title: Defense-Tech Firm Lyntris Shares Plunge 11% After Downsized IPO
item.description: Lyntris Inc. shares fell 11% in its trading debut, after the company and some of its shareholders raised $297.5 million in a downsized initial public offering.

item.title: Jefferies Targets €1 Billion for Private Credit Secondaries Fund
item.description: Jefferies Credit Partners is seeking to raise around €1 billion ($1.16 billion) from investors who trade private credit in the secondary market.

item.title: Iceland Central Banker Urges Government to Rein in Cost Pressure
item.description: Iceland’s central bank chief wants the government to restrain the public sector from linking its fees to inflation to avoid a further increase in western Europe’s highest borrowing costs.

item.title: Copper Firm KME Is Said to Pick Banks for Unit’s German IPO
item.description: KME Group Spa has picked banks to help arrange a Frankfurt listing of Cunova GmbH, which could value the unit producing copper-nickel at as much as €1 billion ($1.2 billion), according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: SDC Capital Is Said to Consider $1 Billion Singapore REIT IPO
item.description: US digital infrastructure firm SDC Capital Partners is planning a real estate investment trust listing in Singapore that could raise about $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: US 10-Year Treasury Yield Will Top 5% This Year: Markets Pulse
item.description: The recent selloff in US bonds that’s sent 30-year yields to multi-decade highs is poised to set another milestone, with the majority of respondents to the latest Markets Pulse survey predicting the 10-year benchmark will soon exceed 5%.

item.title: Citi Turns Bullish on Zambia Debt as Election Heralds Upgrades
item.description: Citigroup Inc. plans to go long on Zambia’s bonds as it sees the copper-producer to be in line for credit upgrades after recent elections.

item.title: Strategic Value Partners Considers Sale of APCOA Parking
item.description: Strategic Value Partners is considering a sale of APCOA Parking Holdings, which could fetch €2 billion ($2.3 billion) to €2.5 billion, people familiar with the matter said.
